1. Shuttle 3-in-a-Row (Shuttle Automatic Win): If a pebble is pushed to an open station to form a 3-in-a-row (Mill) and on its next step can return to its previous station (or an adjacent open station) to form another 3-in-a-row, it can capture all opponent pieces and wins immediately under the Automatic Rule! 2. Double 3-in-a-Row (Double Mill): If a single move forms a 3-in-a-row in two directions simultaneously, it wins immediately. 3. Blockade & 2-Time Forced Unblocking Rule (Rule 4.18 & 4.20): • If a player has captured 2 or more pebbles and blocks all of the opponent's moves, they immediately win by blockade. • However, if a player blocks the opponent before capturing 2 pebbles, the blocking player is ordered to remove a 1st pebble to open a path. If still blocked, they are ordered to remove 1 pebble for a 2nd time. If a path opens, play continues; if still blocked after 2 removals, the blocked player immediately loses the match!

Article 1 — Definition & Historical Origin of Shah Sport

[1.1] Definition: Shah is a strategic traditional board game in which players from two opposing teams sit face-to-face with the game board between them, using foresight and tactical reasoning in accordance with the rules to align their pebbles into rows of 3, capture the opponent\'s pebbles from any chosen station, and block the opponent\'s remaining pebbles from moving to achieve victory.\n[1.2] Historical Background: Widely practiced in Ethiopia—especially across the eastern regions (Somali Region, Dire Dawa, and Oromia)—it is called \"Shatranj\" in Arabic, \"Shantarat\" in Somali, and \"Senterej / Shah\" in Amharic.

[2.1.1] Board Preparation: May be crafted from wood, cardboard, paper, plastic, or similar durable materials.
[2.1.2] Pebble Preparation: Made from wood, plastic, or aluminum-like materials in square or flat circular shapes.
[2.1.3] Board Size & Structure:
• 2.1.3.1: The playing board measures 40 × 40 cm in length and width.
• 2.1.3.2: It is square-shaped and divided into 3 concentric squares decreasing in size from outer to inner.
• 2.1.3.3: The spacing between each concentric square is 5 cm.
• 2.1.3.4: The first (outermost) square must be painted Green, the second (middle) square Yellow, and the third (innermost) square Red.
• 2.1.3.5 – 2.1.3.8: The board has 8 vertical and 8 horizontal lines drawn in black, with 3 stations per line (for a total of 24 pebble placement stations).
[2.1.4] Pebble Size & Quantity: Each pebble must have a radius not exceeding 1 cm, in two distinct colors contrasting with the board: 24 playing pebbles (12 per player) plus 4-4 (8 reserve pebbles), totaling 32 pebbles.

[3.1.1] A team competes by presenting only one (1) competitor for a match.\n[3.1.2] The player who begins the tournament continues as the team\'s competitor through to the final matches.\n[3.2.1] A competitor must compete wearing traditional attire that reflects the culture of their region or locality.
Article 4 — Rules & Procedures of Play (4.1 to 4.22)

[4.1–4.4] Players sit face-to-face with the board between them. To start the pebble placement phase, the referee conducts a lot draw in the 1st and 3rd rounds.
[4.5–4.6] The player who wins the lot places the first pebble on any chosen station; both players then alternate placing their 12–12 pebbles one by one until all 24 are placed.
[4.7–4.9] The player who first forms a 3-in-a-row alignment during placement starts the match. If neither player forms a 3-in-a-row during placement, the player who did NOT win the placement lot starts the match. The starter removes 1 opponent pebble, the second player removes 1 opponent pebble, and then the player who removed the first pebble makes the first sliding move into an open station.
[4.10–4.13] During movement, aligning 3 pebbles vertically or horizontally along a line captures 1 opponent pebble. If a player creates a repeating shuttle 3-in-a-row (Automatic) or Double Mill with that pebble, they win immediately.
[4.15–4.16] Pebbles move only by sliding along a connecting line to an adjacent empty station; jumping over stations or moving diagonally is strictly prohibited.
[4.18–4.20] Blocking & Forced Unblocking Rule: If a player has captured 2 or more pebbles and completely blocks the opponent's moves, they win immediately by blockade. However, if a blockade occurs before capturing 2 pebbles, the blocking player is ordered to remove a 1st pebble to open a path; if still blocked, they must remove a 2nd pebble; if the opponent remains blocked even after the 2nd pebble is removed, the blocked player loses the round!
[4.21–4.22] The thinking time limit for each move is strictly 30 seconds. A 5-minute rest interval is given between rounds.

[5.1] Scoring System: A Shah match is decided by the Best of 3 sets. Winning a set awards 2 points; winning by forfeit (after waiting 10 minutes) also awards 2 points.\n[5.2] Match Completion: A round ends when an opponent is reduced to fewer than 3 pebbles (2 remaining), or when their pebbles are legally blocked from making any move.\n[6.1–6.2] Prohibited Acts & Cards: Distracting the opponent, disputing the referee\'s decision, or violating rules results in verbal warnings for the 1st–3rd fouls, a Yellow Card on the 4th foul, and a Red Card on the 5th foul or for severe misconduct.
Articles 7, 8 & 9 — Duties of Coaches, Team Leaders & Referees

[7.1–7.2] Coaches & Team Leaders: Must arrive at the venue with competitors 30 minutes before the match starts, advise players only during official break intervals, and abide by all competition rules.\n[8.1] Main Referee Duties: Arrive 30 minutes early, inspect playing equipment and ID cards, enforce the 30-second move timer, and preside over the match.\n[8.2] Scorer Referee Duties: Track captured pebbles, record match scores and sign the score sheet alongside the Main Referee, and step in to officiate if the Main Referee is unable to continue.
1. What are the exact length and width of the Shah sport playing board?
According to Article 2.1.3.1, the length and width of the Shah playing board are 40 × 40 cm.
2. What is the spacing in centimeters between the three concentric squares on the Shah board?
According to Article 2.1.3.3, the spacing between each concentric square is 5 cm.
3. What colors must the three concentric squares of the Shah board be painted from outermost (largest) to innermost (smallest)?
According to Article 2.1.3.4, the outermost square is painted Green, the middle square Yellow, and the innermost square Red.
4. How many vertical and horizontal lines and how many pebble placement stations does a Shah board have?
According to Articles 2.1.3.5 and 2.1.3.8, the board has 8 vertical and 8 horizontal black lines and 24 pebble placement stations.
5. What is the total number of playing and reserve pebbles required for an official Shah competition?
According to Article 2.1.4.3, there must be 24 playing pebbles plus 4-4 (8) reserve pebbles, totaling 32 pebbles.
24 playing pebbles and 4-4 reserves of each color (Total 32)
6. What is the maximum allowed size (radius) of Shah playing pebbles?
According to Article 2.1.4.1, Shah playing pebbles must not exceed a 1 cm radius.
7. How many competitors does a team field in a Shah match?
According to Article 3.1.1, a team competes by fielding only one (1) competitor.
8. How many referees officiate a Shah match and what are their roles?
According to Article 8, the match is officiated by 1 Main Referee and 1 Scorer Referee (2 referees in total).
9. How many minutes before the start of the competition must the Main Referee and Scorer Referee arrive at the venue?
According to Articles 8.1.1 and 8.2.1, they must be present at the competition venue 30 minutes before the start.
10. In which rounds (sets) does the referee conduct a lot draw to determine who starts placing pebbles?
According to Article 4.3, a lot draw is conducted in the 1st and 3rd sets of the match.
11. After both players place all 12-12 pebbles on the board, if neither player formed a 3-in-a-row during placement, who starts the game by removing 1 opponent pebble?
According to Article 4.8, if neither player forms a 3-in-a-row during placement, the player who did not win the placement lot starts the game.
The player who won the placement lot draw
The player who did NOT win the placement lot (who placed second)
A new lot draw is held
12. At the start of play, after the first player removes 1 opponent pebble and the second player also removes 1 pebble, who makes the first sliding move into an open station?
According to Article 4.9, after both players remove one pebble each, the player who removed the first pebble slides their own pebble into an open station first.
The player who won the lot
The player who removed the second pebble
The player who removed the first pebble
13. Under the Automatic Instant Win Rule (Shuttle 3-in-a-Row), when does a player win immediately?
When a single pebble can shuttle between two stations forming a 3-in-a-row at both positions, it can capture all opponent pebbles and therefore wins immediately by the Automatic Rule.
When placing all 12 pebbles on the board
When a moved pebble forms a 3-in-a-row that can shuttle back and forth between two stations forming 3-in-a-row on both sides (or a Double Mill)
14. If a player blocks all of the opponent\'s moves without having captured 2 pebbles, and after removing 1 pebble the opponent is STILL blocked, what happens?
Under the Blocking & Forced Unblocking Rule, if removing the 1st pebble does not open a path, a 2nd pebble is removed; if still blocked after 2 pebbles are removed, the blocked player loses.
The blocking player is ordered to remove 1 pebble a 2nd time; if opened, play continues, but if still blocked after the 2nd removal, the blocked player loses the round
The match stops immediately as a draw
The round restarts from the beginning
15. At least how many pebbles must a player have captured to win immediately when completely blocking the opponent\'s moves?
According to Article 4.18, a player who has captured 2 or more pebbles and completely blocks the opponent\'s path wins immediately.
16. During a Shah match, what is the thinking time limit allowed for a player per turn?
According to Article 4.21, the thinking time limit for a player to make a move is strictly 30 seconds.
17. A round ends in victory for the opponent when a player\'s pebbles on the board fall below what number?
According to Article 4.19, if a player\'s pebbles fall below 3 (only 2 remaining), they can no longer form a 3-in-a-row and lose the round.
Only when all pebbles are captured
18. How many minutes of rest are given to players after the completion of each set (round) in Shah?
According to Article 4.22, a 5-minute rest period is given after the end of each set.
19. If a competitor fails to appear at the venue at the scheduled match time, after how many minutes of waiting do they lose by forfeit?
According to Article 5.2.2, if a player does not appear after a 10-minute wait, they lose by forfeit and the opponent is awarded 2 points.
20. Under the Shah foul and penalty rules, on which foul numbers is a player shown a Yellow Card and a Red Card?
Under the penalty rules, fouls 1–3 receive warnings, the 4th foul results in a Yellow Card, and the 5th foul results in a Red Card.
Yellow on 2nd foul, Red on 3rd foul
Yellow Card on 4th foul, Red Card on 5th foul
Yellow on 3rd foul, Red on 4th foul
Yellow on 1st foul, Red on 2nd foul
